newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end higher, block trades seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end higher, block trades seen.

text.p: Singapore shares ended higher in light dealings on Wednesday.

Dealers said the market was quiet with block trades seen in selected counters. Malaysia's KLI Holdings saw a block of 11 million shares changing hands at S$1.574 to S$1.579 about half an hour before the close. It rose seven cents to S$1.80.
"The share price rose after the block deal but there is not much news on what might be happening here," said a broker.
Light buying in selected index stocks pushed the benchmark Straits Times Industrial index up by 19.26 points to 2,195.78. Volume was 81.99 million units with 163 gainers and 137 losers.
Index blue chips like Cerebos Pacific, Fraser & Neave and Keppel Corp rose between 40 and 20 Singapore cents each.
HK Land Holdings fell 10 cents to US$2.77 in active volume of 3.6 million shares. Dealers said the stock was easing after the covered warrants issued on it by two broking houses.
Scotts Holdings saw a block of two million changing hands at S$1.24. It ended up two cents, at S$1.27.

Singapore Telecom ended down eight cents, at S$3.22 on over 2.3 million. Dealers said SingTel will face keen competition when its monopoly on mobile telephones ends in 1997. Other losers included SingLand and CityDev. -- Doreen Siow 65-8703080
